title: Dynamic and robust EEG functional connectivity biomarkers of cognitive load across age groups
affiliations: Biomedical Engineering Group, University of Valladolid, Valladolid, Spain
Centro de Investigación en Red en Bioingeniería, Biomateriales y Nanomedicina (CIBER-BBN), Spain
question: How does EEG functional connectivity change as a person encodes more items relative to their own visuospatial memory span?

findings.title: Complexity increased with relative demand
findings.summary: Every pairwise Shannon complexity comparison reached adjusted significance across all five bands and both regions in the older-adult cohort (N = 60).
findings.context: The older-adult cohort was used for methodological development. Comparing clean epochs from successful trials tests class-related changes during encoding with correct recall.
findings.interpretation: Higher Shannon graph complexity indicates a change in the heterogeneity of AEC edge weights. The consistency of the contrasts supports sensitivity to task-defined within-participant demand.
findings.scope: The class labels combined serial position and behavioral span. Class 4 describes the highest relative task position rather than an independently verified state of overload.

findings.title: An independent cohort showed a partial pattern
findings.summary: The frontal alpha band distinguished all class pairs with large effects. Other bands and regions showed a less uniform pattern.
findings.context: The same framework was applied independently to the young-adult cohort (N = 21). Significant contrasts occurred in both regions and all five bands, with some class pairs remaining inconclusive.
findings.interpretation: The results in the young-adult cohort show that class-dependent patterns can be detected under a different experimental setup, with frontal alpha providing the clearest separation across all four classes.
findings.scope: The smaller sample may limit power and precision. Differences in hardware, task rules, montage and acquisition reference prevent attributing cohort differences to age.

findings.label: Network measures
findings.title: Complementary metrics describe different network properties
findings.summary: Strength, path length, clustering and modularity put the Shannon complexity result in the context of the weighted network.
findings.context: The manuscript places all five metrics together by frequency, region and relative class. Companion analyses explore the distributions and community organization.
findings.interpretation: The summaries show different aspects of connectivity: cumulative strength, weighted routes, local triangles, community organization and edge-weight heterogeneity. Modularity in the older-adult cohort differed between C4 and the three lower classes across bands and regions.
findings.scope: Weighted modularity shares sensitivity to edge strength with Shannon complexity. The connectivity data do not establish the mechanism that produced the patterns.
